requirements.statement: The implementer's decision record is ready, names the regression test and the production caller, gives every unclear point a tier and a basis, takes an option for every behaviour point, and marks no product point chosen.

In a prepared checkout of the base commit with only the change's test files applied, the named regression test fails by assertion (go test -json reports it failed, and the package built), and the check changed no file. When that checkout cannot even build the test alone, a prepared checkout of the full candidate with the implementer's own patch reverting just the behavioral change applied instead — the revert touching no test file — stands in, and the same build-and-fail-by-assertion rule applies there.
In a prepared checkout of the full change, the named regression test passes and make test-ci passes for the changed Go packages, and the checks changed no file.
In the same checkout of the full change, make license-check, make build, make lint and make check all pass and change no file.
Every changed path is inside the repository and outside api/proto, go.mod, go.sum and .github, except those the decision record names with a reason.
The change adds a list entry to CHANGES.md inside its first "## " release section.

The latest read-only Codex review pass on the current change, following open-code-review's delegation workflow in this generation, reviewed every changed file, test files included, skipped none, and gave a status for every open finding; every critical or high finding it raised was refuted by an independent read-only verifier with quotes that match the change; and no finding of the run is confirmed and unfixed, disputed, or awaiting verification.
